name: Heron's Head Park
summary_en: Heron's Head is a park the city has largely paid other people to run. The Port Commission's minutes of 2004 record an authorisation to issue a request for proposals for education and public participation programmes here, and an amendment to the contract with Literacy for Environmental Justice to provide them, with the director's recommendation noting that community participation had been an important part of the park since its inception and a major contributor to its health. Four years later the commission was approving a licence allowing the same organisation to run grant-funded education and habitat improvement programmes on the site, and by 2013 it was issuing a request for proposals to lease the park's EcoCenter together with 6,058 square feet of non-exclusive licence area around it. The park is also a fixture of the working waterfront's calendar — the commission's announcements list it among the sites cleaned on Coastal Cleanup Day, alongside Warm Water Cove, Agua Vista Park and Mission Creek — and its entrance appears in the Port's waterfront parks bond programme beside Crane Cove Park and the Islais Creek shoreline. The money follows the documents exactly: Literacy for Environmental Justice has been paid $256,154.41 between 2021 and 2023.

Ann Lazarus Monique Moyer Executive Director M Request for authorization to issue a Request for Proposals for education and public participation programs at Heron's Head Park. DIRECTOR'S RECOMMENDATION: AUTHORIZE STAFF TO ISSUE A REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS TO PROVIDE EDUCATION AND PUBLIC PARTICIPATION PROGRAMS AT HERON'S HEAD PARK. Background Community participation has been an important part of Heron's Head Park since its inception, and is a major contributor to the health and vitality of the park. Heron's Head Park offers a unique opportunity for local schools and other visitors to study and enjoy wetlands in their own backyard. The Port has sought to actively promote community involvement at the park and to help local schools take advantage of the hands-on educational experience available at Heron's Head Park. To that end, Port staff initially combined efforts with the City College of San Francisco Center for Habitat Restoration, to develop and conduct school and community participation programs at Herons Head Park from 1998 through 2000. This work was funded by a federal grant to City College. During that period, a part-time Park Coordinator with expertise in environmental education and wetland ecology developed a variety of programs for schools and community groups in the vicinity of Heron's Head Park, and for City College students.
